title: Payable days computes exactly, though the definition itself carries no direction
note: payable_days = payables / cost_of_goods_sold * 365 = 30 / 120 * 365 = 91.25 days, within the plausible band [0, 180]. The arithmetic here is not in dispute -- see disputed_reason for what is.
disputed_reason: RatioDefinition('payable_days').direction_hint is None in domain/ratios/definitions.py, i.e. the library takes no position on which side of a payable-days covenant is a breach. Indian sanction letters that covenant payable days always cap it as a maximum (a lengthening payable cycle is the deterioration signal), so this example's hand label is that a bank-authored payable_days covenant should default to direction='max' when intake proposes one. The implementation is right until this is decided by a human: it is a considered 'no opinion' for a value the library also does not itself compare against a threshold, so it is recorded here rather than silently patched.
